Ah. Well definitely give the original a test run then (free on his site) using the robot or alien. Robot's pretty sturdy but has the same objectives/abilities as the human, he only has to worry about the xenos and battery power.

You can build things with the materials you scavenge like battery-operated turrets or a small personal shielding system. They can be picked up and redeployed as you move, so you can drag one with you if you're going somewhere dangerous. The human is an engineer, so you can do more advanced things than just rig up makeshift zip guns or molotovs and flares, and the robot being the copilot had all his general knowledge programmed in. Human is the roughest due to needing to manage climate, food, protection, and water, but can put out the most damage in the endgame. The robot's hampered by having to share its "food meter" with energy weapons and the turret, should you construct those. But it can survive quite a beating, the alien queen has to be on you about 15 seconds to kill you, her kids fare nowhere near as well.

The xeno would be second easiest I'd say, due to not much management being needed, and evolving as you kill more difficult enemy xenos. (one possible ending for it is to become the new queen rather than escape)

The psionic can only build the first tier of objects and a couple from the second, but essentially has force powers, slightly better night vision, and slower digestion. (in full moon don't need flashlight) Can avoid most fights after awhile.

as you can see from the video trailer though, and his own playthrough you're intended to go through it Alien: Isolation style to get the full suspense effect, so in a way after figuring out the RNG (or being blessed by it ie the destroyed radar facility or storage warehouse spawns near you) you get to adjust the difficulty yourself. The more you protect yourself the longer the quest takes, as you use up parts that could go on the shuttle. Pretty nifty way of handling it.

The world map is...I think it was 5 x 5 "rooms" 4x4 screens each, not counting enterable areas. The center room and four farthest away are always the same, but everything in between is randomly generated (hence RNG mention). It's possible to beat it your first time out, but not likely. (The robot's biggest problem being spawning next to the warehouse, as he uh, doesn't "eat" organic matter, haha.) Probably 70%+ of robot deaths will be due to "Where are the fucking batteries?!?!"

Might be a good idea to 'cheat' and scum it, and just take off straight in one direction.

Oh yeah speaking of adjusting your difficulty, you will no doubt need to find this on an abandonware site somewhere, but remember those guys that made the infamous flying windows screensaver, Software Dynamics? Just remembered they made a really nice top-down spaceflight RPG called Inner Space, it's from waaaay back in the mid-90s, but the gist is your computer is "space" and executables, batch files, icons, and the like, are collectible objects and traded in for currency at the starbases, other files become asteroids or space junk, and your folders function as the stages, or 'quadrants.' Difficulty resets each folder, so the bigger it is the harder it'll get. Also how much trouble you cause or how many enemies you make of the various space clans adjusts how hard the start and ends are. (also if you're a felon you'll basically be facing Oblivion guards, the cops don't obey the difficulty reset rule, and can even follow you across different folders) It's kinda sad how little that ever came up as a game mechanic, it's really fun.
